facts.text: Patterson sprang up in 1846 when the Big Four Railroad cut through the forest, turning the village into a bustling lumber and grain hub.
In 1848 Isaiah Ickes opened a tannery, and by 1863 a warehouse had been converted into a grist mill that fed the growing community.
Patterson Field was renamed in 1931, becoming part of the larger Wright‑Patterson Air Force Base that today hosts the 88th Air Base Wing.
Along P Street in Patterson lie Adena culture mounds, prehistoric earthworks that once marked the territory of ancient Native American peoples.
The 88th Air Base Wing, stationed at Wright‑Patterson, employs more than 5,000 officers, enlisted airmen, civilians and contractors who keep the base running.
